findings.title: Web project directly references Infrastructure layer — SQLitePCL init and ContestDbContext resolved in UI startup
findings.rule_violated: Clean Architecture: Dependency Rule — outer layers (Web) must not depend on inner layers (Infrastructure) for anything except DI composition
findings.remediation: 1) Remove Infrastructure ProjectReference and EF Core/SQLite PackageReferences from Web.csproj. 2) Move SQLitePCL.Batteries_V2.Init() into ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddContestJudgingServices(). 3) Replace direct ContestDbContext resolution in Program.cs with an IDatabaseInitializer abstraction or move database restore into Services. 4) Web should only call builder.Services.AddContestJudgingServices() as its single composition entry point.

findings.title: ContestManager (Services/Application layer) directly depends on concrete ContestDbContext from Infrastructure
findings.rule_violated: SOLID: Dependency Inversion Principle — high-level modules (Services/ContestManager) must not depend on low-level modules (Infrastructure/ContestDbContext); both should depend on abstractions. Clean Architecture: inner layers must not know about outer layer concretions.
findings.remediation: 1) Extract an IDatabaseBackupService interface (export/import byte array) into Core.Interfaces. 2) Implement DatabaseBackupService in Infrastructure with raw file I/O. 3) Have ContestManager depend on IDatabaseBackupService instead of ContestDbContext. 4) Remove ExportDatabaseAsync/ImportDatabaseAsync from ContestDbContext (fixing ARCH-004). 5) Update tests to use the mockable IDatabaseBackupService abstraction.

findings.title: Service interfaces (IValidationService, IPartitionService, IGlobalRankingService, IContestManager) defined in Services project instead of Core
findings.rule_violated: SOLID: Dependency Inversion Principle — abstractions should be owned by the policy-defining layer (Core or Application.Abstractions), not the implementation layer. Clean Architecture: Dependency Rule — all compile-time dependencies point inward.
findings.remediation: 1) Move IValidationService, IPartitionService, IGlobalRankingService, and IContestManager to ContestJudging.Core.Interfaces. 2) Update using directives in all implementations and Web consumers. 3) Consider a separate ContestJudging.Core.Interfaces.Services sub-namespace or a ContestJudging.Application.Abstractions project for service-level abstractions distinct from domain abstractions.

findings.title: ContestDbContext violates Single Responsibility — mixes ORM configuration with raw file I/O export/import
findings.rule_violated: SOLID: Single Responsibility Principle — a class should have only one reason to change. ContestDbContext should change only when the data model changes, not when the backup persistence mechanism changes. Clean Code: separation of concerns — data access and file I/O backup are distinct responsibilities that should not be co-located.
findings.remediation: 1) Move ExportDatabaseAsync and ImportDatabaseAsync into a dedicated DatabaseBackupService class in Infrastructure. 2) Inject database path via configuration instead of hardcoding 'contest.db'. 3) Register IDatabaseBackupService in DI. 4) Remove these methods from ContestDbContext entirely. This also enables fixing ARCH-002 by giving ContestManager a mockable abstraction for backup operations.

findings.title: Composition root (ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddContestJudgingServices) in Services layer instead of outermost layer
findings.rule_violated: Clean Architecture Composition Root pattern — the composition root should be as close to the application entry point (the outermost layer, Web) as possible. Only the entry-point assembly should reference all other assemblies. Inner layers should not need knowledge of concrete implementations from outer layers.
findings.remediation: 1) Move ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddContestJudgingServices to the Web project (or a Web DI folder). 2) Remove the Services → Infrastructure project reference. 3) Services should only reference Core and define interfaces there (see ARCH-003). 4) Register all implementations from the Web composition root, where references to all projects are natural.

findings.title: Two IScoringStrategy implementations exist but are never registered in DI container
findings.rule_violated: Principle of Least Surprise — multiple strategy implementations exist but only one is wired in DI. If the alternatives are dead code they should be removed; if they're live, they should be selectable via configuration. YAGNI — code that ships but can never be reached from the application entry point is dead weight.
findings.remediation: 1) If PercentileScoring and DefinedIntervalScoring are production features: add a configuration mechanism (enum, settings key) to select the active scoring strategy at startup. 2) For DefinedIntervalScoring, implement a factory registration that reads rank points from configuration. 3) If they are legacy/experimental: delete the unused implementation files and their tests.

findings.title: AddScoped DbContext lifetime in Blazor WASM — DbContext effectively singleton, change tracker grows unbounded
findings.rule_violated: EF Core best practices — DbContext instances should be short-lived per unit-of-work. In Blazor WASM, AddDbContextFactory<T> should be used to create short-lived contexts per operation, or ChangeTracker.Clear() should be called periodically to prevent unbounded memory growth.
findings.remediation: 1) Replace AddDbContext<ContestDbContext> with AddDbContextFactory<ContestDbContext>. 2) Update repositories to inject IDbContextFactory<ContestDbContext> and create/dispose DbContext per operation. 3) Alternatively, call context.ChangeTracker.Clear() after batch operations (e.g., after CalculateGlobalScoresAsync in ContestManager). 4) The startup database restore in Program.cs should create a temporary context and dispose it immediately.

findings.title: No consistent rule for interface placement — repository interfaces in Core, service interfaces in Services
findings.rule_violated: Architecture consistency — mixed interface placement strategies create confusion for developers and make onboarding harder. A single, documented rule should govern where interfaces live.
findings.remediation: 1) Adopt a single rule: all interfaces go in Core (ContestJudging.Core.Interfaces). 2) Move IValidationService, IPartitionService, IGlobalRankingService, and IContestManager to Core. 3) Document the rule in AGENTS.md or the project README under an 'Architecture' section. 4) Consider a Core.Interfaces.Services sub-namespace or a dedicated Application.Abstractions project for service-level interfaces to distinguish them from domain abstractions.
